text:
maya: quick question — we're about to roll out the visibility sampling for multi-tenant quotas. how do people feel about exposing sampled request attrs in console telemetry vs keeping them server-side only? :thinking:

alex: i'd prefer server-side only for PII reasons. sampling helps, but console previews should show aggregated metrics not raw attrs.

jordan: agreed re PII. but we need enough context to debug per-tenant anomalies (model, route, request_size). can we surface redacted fields? e.g. model name + bucketed token_count?

maya: yeah redaction + bucketing is what i was thinking. also wondering about sampling rate. current plan: 1% global by default, 10% for flagged cohorts during dry-run. thoughts?

sasha: 1% seems low for low-traffic tenants — might not capture signals. maybe sample by request type: sample more for long tails (long seqs) and error responses. heuristics: if latency > P95 OR status != 200, upsampling to 20%.

alex: +1 to upsampling on anomalies. but we need to be careful with cost. could we do a two-pass: cheap meta-sample first (headers, model_id, duration) then pull full payload for selected samples?

maya: good call. two-pass pipeline makes sense. console UX question: how do we label sampled data vs full logs? want product to know the caveats.

tanya: from compliance side: require an opt-out toggle per-org for sampled payloads. default off for enterprise until legal signs off. console should show a clear badge: "sampled data" and link to policy.

jordan: API changes needed: add ?sample_detail=meta|full to /telemetry/query and a header X-Sample-Id. example:```GET /telemetry/query?start=...&sample_detail=meta Accept: application/json X-Sample-Id: abc123```That keeps it explicit.

sasha: love the header. also include sample_reason in meta: e.g. {"trigger":"latency_p95","policy":"dry_run_cohort"}. helps triage.

deploy-bot: config applied to canary: visibility_sampling.default_rate=0.01; visibility_sampling.upsample_on_error=0.2; dryrun_cohort_rate=0.1 — rollout id r-2026-03-21-01

maya: ok next steps: 1) implement two-pass pipeline API + header; 2) console flags for org-level opt-out + badge copy; 3) telemetry schema: include sample_reason + redaction marker; 4) document cost estimate for ops. can we get rough numbers by EOD? :eyes:

alex: i'll run cost sim on sample sizes and upsampling heuristics and post numbers here.

jordan: i'll draft API spec PR and include example queries and error-handling for missing sample ids.

sasha: i'll wire up the upsample trigger rules in the selector service and add unit tests for edge cases (batching + upsample overlap).

tanya: i'll prepare the compliance checklist and necessary opt-out legal text draft.

maya: thanks. quick follow-up — should dry-run cohort default to 10% or 5%? deploy-bot suggested 10% in canary. any objections?

alex: prefer 5% initially to keep cost low, but set ramp automation to 10% if no anomaly in 24h.

jordan: fine with that. we'll add a ramp rule: increase 5->10 after 24h no anomalies, rollback on anomaly signal.

maya: perfect. i'll update the rollout doc and open the console copy ticket. thanks all.
